guidance.intro: This is the first thing families and gamers see of you.

do.you: Just you, head and shoulders, face clearly visible
do.light: Soft, even light, for example facing a window
do.natural: Relaxed and natural: look like yourself
do.gear: A headset or controller in the shot is fine

dont.others: Anyone else in the frame. For safeguarding, a photo with a child in it can’t be used
dont.hidden: Sunglasses, masks or anything hiding your face
dont.group: Group shots, or yourself cropped out of one

about.heading: About you
about.title: Title
about.titleHint: Your job at School of Gaming, for example Head of Clubs.

writing.heading: In your own words

guidance.lead: Once the profile is public, it appears on the Team page of School of Gaming’s website, where both gamers and parents read it. Parents often want to know who leads their child’s sessions, what kind of person they are and what matters to them when working with children and young people.
guidance.thirdPerson: Write the bio in the third person, like an introduction, but let it sound like the person it introduces rather than a CV.

dont.cv: A CV or a long list of facts
dont.jokes: Inside jokes a new reader won’t get

ideas.intro: There is no single right way to write a profile, and no two need look alike. If getting started is hard, these questions can help.

questions.games: What kinds of games do you enjoy, and why?
questions.memory: Is there a game, gaming memory or community that has been especially meaningful to you?
questions.outside: What do you enjoy doing outside of work or gaming?
questions.players: What do you value when working with players?
questions.atmosphere: What kind of atmosphere do you want to create?
questions.why: Why is game education meaningful to you?
questions.topics: Are there particular topics or skills you are especially interested in?
questions.background: Is there something from your own background that influences the way you work?

writing.languagesHint: The website doesn’t translate the profile. Add each language it should appear in, and write it under that language’s tab.
writing.bioTooLong: The bio is too long to save. Shorten it to {max} characters or fewer.
writing.longDescriptionHint: In the third person, like an introduction.
writing.longDescriptionPlaceholder: Anna has led clubs since 2023 and loves teaching redstone.
writing.funFactPlaceholder: Once built a working calculator in Minecraft.
